description: `apply_update` advances the Lamport counter past every observed op — unconditionally, and BEFORE the idempotence skip — so a write minted AFTER a sync outranks everything the sync delivered. Replica `b` reorders a leaf six times, driving its top dot to (9, 2) and leaving `y`'s sort stamp at (9, 2); `b` syncs into `a`, and only THEN does `a` reorder. A binding that advances its counter on ingest mints (10, 1), which beats (9, 2) under the (counter, peer) order, so the post-sync reorder wins on `a` and again on `b` after the return sync — both render `xy`. A binding that leaves its counter untouched mints (4, 1) instead: that loses the LWW comparison against the stamp (9, 2) it just ingested, so its own local reorder is rejected on `a` and on `b`, and both render `yx`. Note the failure is symmetric — both replicas still CONVERGE on the wrong text — so `converged` alone cannot see it and `render_on` is the load-bearing assertion. No pre-existing lossless-tree fixture could discriminate this, because every one of them is fork -> concurrent edits -> sync, and never mutates a replica AFTER a sync into it. Motivated by lazily-cpp `fb9fc80` (#lzcppapplyupdatelamport), whose `apply_update` never advanced the counter.
